meta.system: Smart Coriander Cultivation and Quality Monitoring System
meta.status_note: Entries marked "verify" are working values chosen for the dataset-driven prototype. Confirm them against ICAR / Spices Board / your state agricultural university package of practices (and against sensor calibration) before any field use.
meta.sensor_note: NPK values are in mg/kg as reported by an RS-485 soil NPK probe. Such probes are indicative, not lab-grade.

n.label: Nitrogen (N)
n.basis: Working sufficiency bands derived from the Indian soil-fertility rating classes for available N (low below ~280 kg/ha, converted at ~2.24 kg/ha per mg/kg), raised in the vegetative stage when N demand is highest.
n.excess_advice: Nitrogen is already high. Skip nitrogen fertilizer at this stage; extra N promotes leafy growth and lodging and can delay seed maturity.

p.label: Phosphorus (P)
p.basis: Working bands above the Indian 'low' class for available P (about 10 kg/ha, roughly 4.5 mg/kg); P is weighted higher at germination (root establishment) and flowering (seed set).
p.excess_advice: Phosphorus is already high. Skip phosphatic fertilizer this cycle.

k.label: Potassium (K)
k.basis: Working bands above the Indian 'low' class for available K (about 120 kg/ha, roughly 54 mg/kg); K is weighted higher toward seed filling.
k.excess_advice: Potassium is already high. Skip potash fertilizer this cycle.

moisture.label: Soil moisture
moisture.basis: Volumetric water content (%). Needs sensor-specific calibration. Higher at germination, drier toward ripening.
moisture.low_advice: Soil is dry. Irrigate lightly and evenly.
moisture.high_advice: Soil is too wet. Hold irrigation and check drainage (waterlogging risk).

temperature.label: Temperature
temperature.basis: Coriander prefers a cool climate while vegetative and a warmer, dry climate at flowering.
temperature.low_advice: Cold stress. Growth will slow; mulch or protect young plants.
temperature.high_advice: Heat stress reduces growth and yield. Irrigate lightly in the evening and mulch to cool the root zone.

ph.label: Soil pH
ph.basis: Coriander grows best in near-neutral, well-drained soil.
ph.low_advice: Soil is acidic. Confirm with a lab test, then consider liming.
ph.high_advice: Soil is alkaline. Add organic matter or gypsum after a lab test; prefer acidifying fertilizers such as DAP.

ec.label: Salinity (EC)
ec.basis: Coriander is sensitive to salinity, most of all at germination.
ec.low_advice: Very low EC suggests little available nutrient.
ec.high_advice: Salinity is high and coriander is salt-sensitive. Leach salts with low-salt irrigation water and avoid muriate of potash (use sulphate of potash).

light.label: Light intensity
light.basis: Evaluated only in the daytime window; night readings are not judged.
light.low_advice: Low midday light. Check for shading or a very dense canopy.

pressure.label: Air pressure
pressure.basis: Informational. A fast fall signals rain or a storm, so the app delays fertilizer application.

wind.label: Wind speed
wind.basis: Strong wind disturbs spraying and can lodge tall flowering plants.
wind.high_advice: Strong wind. Delay urea broadcasting and sprays, and check plants for lodging.

fertilizer_plan.recommended_total_source: ICAR-NRCSS, Ajmer trial on variety ACr-2 (60:30:20 kg NPK/ha). A Karnataka trial reports 60:40:20 as optimal; adjust for your soil and region.
fertilizer_plan.method_note: One corrective application = recommended total dose x corrective fraction x severity multiplier. This avoids converting a probe reading straight into kg/ha, which overstates the need. Multipliers are a working design choice (verify: true).

sources: ICAR-NRCSS Ajmer four-year study, coriander ACr-2: 60:30:20 kg/ha NPK with 30 x 10 cm geometry
Karnataka trials cited in ICAR literature: 60:40:20 kg/ha NPK optimum
Banaras Hindu University soil-test crop response study: 4.83 kg N, 0.80 kg P2O5 and 4.10 kg K2O per quintal of grain (candidate for a future STCR-based dose equation)
PLOS One (2026) STCR prescription equations for coriander in Alfisols: coriander needs a cool climate when vegetative and a warm, dry climate at flowering
Indian soil-fertility rating classes (low / medium / high) for available N, P and K, as used on Soil Health Cards
